stem: For 2 NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), a supplied concentration-based K = 1.00×10⁻⁴ at the stated temperature. Initially [NO₂] = 1.00 M and [N₂O₄] = 0. Let x be [N₂O₄] at equilibrium. For comparison only, an independent numerical solver gives x = 9.99600×10⁻⁵ M; solving a quadratic is not required. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Set up the equilibrium relation and estimate x by neglecting NO₂ depletion.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Check the neglected change and compare the approximation with the supplied numerical result.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain the two stoichiometric mistakes in writing K = x/(1.00−x) and using the same concentration change for both species.

steps.text: If 2 x is negligible beside 1.00, the denominator is approximately 1.00.
Estimated NO₂ depletion = 2 x≈2.00×10⁻⁴ M.
This is 0.0200% of the initial 1.00 M, well below a 5% check.
The approximation differs from 9.99600×10⁻⁵ M by about 0.0400%.

The equilibrium expression also squares [NO₂] because its equation coefficient is 2.
Material changes and equilibrium powers both follow the balanced equation, but play different mathematical roles.

title: Products initially present can force a reverse change
subtopic: How far? The extent of chemical change
stem: For H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2 HI(g), K = 16.0 at a fixed temperature. A mixture has [H₂] = [I₂] = 0.200 M and [HI] = 1.20 M. Let x be the concentration of each reactant formed by net reverse reaction. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why an ICE table must not automatically subtract x from every initial reactant concentration.

4 = (1.20−2 x)/(0.200 + x), with all concentrations positive.
The net direction here is reverse, so species on the left of the written equation increase.
The signs of stoichiometric changes must follow the predicted direction and preserve non-negative concentrations.

title: The container volume cannot be cancelled from every equilibrium
subtopic: How far? The extent of chemical change
stem: At equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2 NO₂(g), the vessel contains 0.0200 mol N₂O₄ and 0.0400 mol NO₂. The numerical constant is K = 0.0800 when concentrations are expressed in mol dm⁻³. The volume is unknown. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for K in terms of the mole amounts and volume V, then determine V.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The volume is halved instantaneously at fixed temperature. Calculate Q immediately afterwards and predict the net direction.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why the original mole ratio alone was insufficient to identify equilibrium for arbitrary V.

steps.text: K = (n NO₂/V)²/(n N₂O₄/V) = n NO₂²/(Vn N₂O₄).
V = 1.00 dm³.
Both concentrations double, so Q is multiplied by 2²/2 = 2.
Net reverse change forms N₂O₄, the side with fewer gas particles.
The total powers of concentration are different on the two sides.
One inverse-volume factor remains after substitution, so the same mole amounts at a different volume can give a different Q.
Kstays fixed at constant temperature; concentrations, not unnormalised mole ratios alone, enter this expression.

title: Expansion lowers every concentration but can favour dissociation
subtopic: How far? The extent of chemical change
stem: For CO(g) + Cl₂(g) ⇌ COCl₂(g), a mixture at equilibrium has [CO] = [Cl₂] = 0.200 M and [COCl₂] = 0.400 M. At 20 s the vessel volume doubles instantly at constant temperature. The constructed traces show subsequent relaxation; no new-equilibrium quadratic calculation is requested. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate K and the reaction quotient immediately after expansion.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the quotient and the graph to explain the net chemical response.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why the initial downward jumps do not themselves represent reaction and why K does not become 20.0.

steps.text: After doubling volume, all concentrations halve:0.100, 0.100, 0.200 M.
Q>K, so net reverse change reduces the excess product-to-reactant ratio.
CO and Cl₂ increase after their instantaneous drops, while COCl₂ decreases further.
Reverse change produces two gas particles per product molecule, consistent with the response to expansion.
The jumps occur from a volume change before appreciable chemical change.
They dilute existing amounts rather than consume them chemically.
K is temperature-dependent and remains 10.0; 20.0 is the transient non-equilibrium quotient.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

title: Two consistent equilibria constrain a third reported constant
subtopic: How far? The extent of chemical change
stem: Three dissolved isomers A, B and C share a molecular formula. At one temperature, A ⇌ B has KAB = [B]/[A] = 2.00 and B ⇌ C has KBC = [C]/[B] = 3.00. A report gives KAC = 5.00 for A ⇌ C. Concentration-based ideal behaviour is assumed. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Derive KAC from the two supplied expressions and evaluate the report.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A closed solution initially contains 0.900 M of A only. Determine all three equilibrium concentrations.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why an intermediate isomer can cancel from an overall equilibrium relation without having zero concentration.

steps.text: Multiply KABKBC = ([B]/[A])([C]/[B]).
B cancels, giving KAC = [C]/[A] = 2.00×3.00 = 6.00.
A reported value 5.00 is inconsistent with the other exact values at the same temperature and convention.
At equilibrium [B] = 2[A] and [C] = 3[B] = 6[A].
Conservation gives [A] + [B] + [C] = 9[A] = 0.900 M.
Cancellation is algebraic between numerator and denominator, not physical removal of B.
Here B has a nonzero equilibrium concentration 0.200 M.
The overall A–C relation describes a ratio while both component equilibria continue to involve B.

title: An equilibrium candidate must satisfy two independent tests
subtopic: How far? The extent of chemical change
stem: For 2 NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), the initial equilibrium concentrations are [NO₂] = 0.400 M, [N₂O₄] = 0.200 M. The volume is halved at unchanged T. Two proposed final concentration pairs([NO₂], [N₂O₄]) are X = (0.600, 0.500) M and Y = (0.800, 0.800) M. Neither pair is guaranteed correct. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate K and the immediate post-compression quotient.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Test candidate X against both equilibrium and nitrogen-atom conservation.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Test Y and explain why satisfying only one condition is insufficient.

steps.text: Immediately concentrations double to 0.800 and 0.400 M.
Qimmediate = 0.400/0.800² = 0.625<K, so net forward change is expected.
After compression the conserved NO₂-equivalent concentration is 0.800 + 2(0.400) = 1.60 M.
X gives 0.600 + 2(0.500) = 1.60 M, so it conserves nitrogen.
But QX = 0.500/0.600² = 1.38889≠1.25; X is not equilibrium.
QY = 0.800/0.800² = 1.25, satisfying the equilibrium expression.
But Y has 0.800 + 2(0.800) = 2.40 M NO₂ equivalents, violating the conserved 1.60 M.
An admissible equilibrium must satisfy both material conservation and the equilibrium law, so both proposed pairs are rejected.

title: Small K does not by itself justify neglecting every concentration change
subtopic: How far? The extent of chemical change
stem: A constructed ideal homogeneous concentration model has A + B ⇌ AB with K = 0.0100. Initially [A] = 1.00×10⁻⁴ M, [B] = 10.0 M, [AB] = 0. Let x = [AB] eq. These supplied idealised data are a mathematical concentration model, not a claim about real non-ideal solutions at 10 M. No quadratic solution is required. Give calculated answers to three significant figures unless a different precision is requested.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Retain A depletion but neglect only the negligible change in B. Solve the resulting linear relation.

parts.label: c

steps.text: This consumes 10.0% of A, so neglecting its change fails a 5% check despite K<1.
Neglecting B depletion is therefore self-consistent in this supplied model.
Approximation quality depends on each reactant’s relative depletion and initial concentrations, not on K alone.
